title: Running the done is the authoritative verdict on a finding
description:
The oracle half of gvc's two-tier rule. Given a finding and the epic's acceptance items, run every item that IS runnable and answer whether the done is reachable with the finding standing.

The rule this establishes, and nothing later may weaken it: where an item can be run, running it WINS. No classifier overrides an observation. A prediction that disagrees with a run is the prediction being wrong, and that is the whole reason the oracle is built first.

The two worked cases from the session gvc came out of, both of which this tier handles:
  - two fixtures made go test -short red at base, so no tick could close behind the gate
    and the done was unreachable. GATING, observed, no judgement needed.
  - ky5 (a merge_failed refusal naming no conflicting file) cost an operator an hour and
    left every acceptance item reachable. NOT GATING, and it correctly stayed backlog.

Record the verdict as OBSERVED, with the item id and the command's evidence, in the
shape gate evidence already takes - keyed by the commit it ran on, so the record means
something on a re-derivation rather than being a timestamped opinion.

Items that are not runnable are NOT this tick's answer. Return them as unresolved and
let the next tick predict them. An oracle that guesses is not an oracle.
acceptance_criteria: Given a finding and an epic's acceptance, every runnable item is run and the finding is reported GATING or NOT GATING as an OBSERVED verdict naming the item and its evidence; unrunnable items come back unresolved rather than assumed either way; the verdict is keyed by the commit it ran on; and go test -short ./... passes
